findings.title: Withdrawal reclaims a peaceful boundary
findings.claim: Within the preceding exchange, Abraham's withdrawal can be heard as reclaiming an imposed expulsion as a deliberate, nonretaliatory boundary while keeping prayerful concern across the separation.
findings.mechanism: The threat of being stoned and the command to leave at 19:46 contact the focus act of setting himself apart; the reply of peace and promised intercession at 19:47 keeps the boundary from becoming reciprocal hostility and lets calling continue across it.
findings.reader_payoff: The exit becomes an act of disciplined agency in response to coercion, not merely a change of location.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains withdrawal from the people and what they invoke besides God in order to call upon the Lord. The agency-preserving and nonretaliatory relation is inferred from the sequence; no general strategy of de-escalation is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic anchors, focus carriers, and contextual coordinates are supplied, but several context branches have no independent registry detail and remain attributed HFT evidence.

findings.title: Withdrawal opens gifted kinship
findings.claim: The pericope lets Abraham's enacted withdrawal stand as a threshold through which unbought kinship and prophetic continuity arrive, so separation is costly without becoming barren.
findings.mechanism: 19:49 repeats the focus separation and immediately places it before gifts of Isaac and Jacob, their made prophetic status, and the mercy and truthful mention of 19:50; the later acts therefore give the focus boundary a generative consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus prayer is newly seen within a movement from relinquished belonging toward a renewed field of relation rather than sterile isolation.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains Abraham's withdrawal from his people and their worship followed by prayer. The compensatory or generative arrow is an inference from the sequence; the verses may also be read as simple narrative succession.

epistemic.reason: The exact repetition, gift, making, prophetic, and mercy surfaces are supplied, but unresolved context branches carry attributed HFT roles and the target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Distance becomes selective proximity
findings.claim: The pericope makes Abraham's distance selective: he is set apart from hostile or false relations while the Lord-relation persists and can be imagined as opening into intimate address.
findings.mechanism: The focus places separation beside the inferior relation expressed by dūn, while 19:47 supplies attentive care and 19:52 places side-distance beside being brought near for confidential converse; distance from one addressee therefore becomes compatible with nearness to another.
findings.reader_payoff: The withdrawal is newly legible as a redistribution of proximity rather than as absolute isolation.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains Abraham's movement away from his people and their invoked objects toward prayer. The Moses pattern is an analogical contextual resonance only: the connection registry records a no-value counterdirection, and no direct identity between the two scenes is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The exact 19:47 and 19:52 surfaces and HFT coordinates are supplied, but target morphology is absent and the reciprocal connection preserves a no-value counterdirection against direct transfer.

findings.title: The abandoned audience becomes durable voice

findings.reader_payoff: Withdrawal no longer looks like the erasure of speech: the audience changes while address remains communicatively productive.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains withdrawal so that Abraham may call upon his Lord. The transfer from rejected local address to durable public testimony is inferred from the framing verses; those honors may also be read independently of the withdrawal.

epistemic.reason: The Book-remembrance, focus calling, and truthful-tongue surfaces are exact, while the context branches for remembrance, writing, tongue, and truthful speech remain attributed and target morphology is absent.

findings.title: Prayer reroutes provision after the cut
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus sequence can hold a provision image in which separation is a cut that reroutes rather than sterilizes relation, while prayer is the retained opening through which nurture returns as gifted lineage.
findings.mechanism: The water-outlet and milk-return facets meet the focus's repeated call and Lord relation, then contact the immediate gift of 19:49 and the mercy relation of 19:50; the material analogy makes renewed provision perceptible after separation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive hope and prayer as a remaining channel through which relation continues, rather than as words detached from the gifts that follow.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains withdrawal from false addressees and hope that prayer to the Lord will not bring misery. The milk, outlet, growth, and womb images are a cross-domain material model, not a claim that the focus words literally denote lactation or fertility.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus facets and pericope coordinates support the analogy, but the branch combination is cross-domain, two context branches are unresolved, and the source explicitly marks the relation exploratory.

findings.title: The Lord address carries authority and account
findings.claim: The individually added 1:4 can also make the focus's Lord address carry an authority of ownership and account: Abraham's hope is voiced toward the one whose rule includes the day of reckoning.
findings.mechanism: The focus Rabb carrier at 19:48:13:1 meets the external owner and judgment occurrences at 1:4:1 and 1:4:3, adding authority and accountability to the Lord-relation after the speaker leaves false addressees.
findings.reader_payoff: The hope not to be made miserable by prayer gains a supplied horizon of accountable rule without ceasing to be a personal plea.
findings.containment: This is a bounded Phase-2 overlay from 1:4 alone. It adds an authority-and-account dimension to the focus prayer; it does not replace the focus's ordinary hope or import the whole external sequence.

epistemic.reason: The external owner and judgment occurrences are supplied exactly, while their contact with the focus Lord address is an authored local inference without a separate support trust label.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Sahiplik, buyruk yetkisi ve yönetip düzenleme aynı çekirdekte birleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The second focus Rabb form at 19:48:13:1 carries the supplied ownership, command, and governance relation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The external owner occurrence at 1:4:1 and judgment/account occurrence at 1:4:3.
branch_activations.activation: The focus Lord carrier contacts the external authority-and-account pair, making the hoped-for prayer answerable within a governed order rather than an unbounded private wish.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speaker's hope remains personal while addressing a Lord whose rule includes account.
branch_activations.boundary: The overlay adds an accountability horizon from 1:4 only; it does not assert a specific judgment of Abraham or replace the focus's plain prayer.

friction_notes: The six assigned HFT records are legacy_unbound: exact Arabic anchors and context coordinates are present, but target morphology and independent branch descriptors are absent for the unresolved branches, so those activations remain attributed and qualified.

The 19:52 distance-to-nearness proposal retains a live analogical alternative because the connection registry includes a no-value reciprocal counterdirection; this does not defeat the supplied HFT trace but limits its directness.

The automatic host basmala and the external ayat were reviewed separately. Only external 1:2 and 1:4 add a specific carrier-trigger delta beyond the pericope; the remaining listed external material did not add a distinct local contact beyond native worship, mercy, guidance, or path relations.
